claims.claim: In June 2008 President Lee Myung-bak directed his land minister to add weirs and deepen dredging on the four major rivers.
claims.episode_span: In June 2008, President Lee Myung-bak directed his land minister to add weirs and deepen dredging on the four major rivers rather than rely on dike reinforcement alone.
claims.source_title: Audit agency: Ex-President Lee's Four Rivers Project shoddily designed
claims.supporting_quote: The project began when Lee suggested it to his land minister in June 2008, two months after he announced he would give up on the grand canal project.

claims.claim: The project cost 22 trillion won and installed 16 weirs between 2008 and 2012.
claims.episode_span: The 22 trillion won project that followed created sixteen concrete structures meant to store water and reduce flood risk.
claims.source_title: Audit agency: Ex-President Lee's Four Rivers Project shoddily designed
claims.supporting_quote: The Lee administration spent 22 trillion won (US$20 billion) from 2008-2012 on the Four Rivers Project

claims.claim: Lee ordered the Nakdong River minimum depth raised to at least 6 meters and total storage set at 800 million tons.
claims.episode_span: Lee issued repeated design orders that raised the minimum depth on the Nakdong River from four to six meters and set a total storage target of 800 million tons.
claims.source_title: Audit agency: Ex-President Lee's Four Rivers Project shoddily designed
claims.supporting_quote: when the ministry reported to Lee that the minimum depth of the Nakdong River running southeast in the country would be set at 4 meters and the river would be able to hold 490 million tons of water, Lee ordered the river's minimum depth should be at least 6 meters. Presidential officials also said the river should be able to hold at least 800 million tons of water.

claims.claim: The Board of Audit and Inspection found higher algae concentrations and chemical oxygen demand in 2012 than the prior five-year average.
claims.episode_span: The Board of Audit and Inspection’s 2013 and 2018 reports recorded higher algae concentrations and chemical oxygen demand across all sixteen reservoirs
claims.source_title: Gov't, ruling party clash over reported flaws in four-rivers project
claims.supporting_quote: the Board of Audit and Inspection (BAI) said in the report that it found higher concentrations of algae and higher chemical oxygen demand (COD) in the water in 2012 compared to the average for the previous five years.
